theorem: Theorem 4.1 (v1 Section 4), stated as Theorem 1.1 in v2
model_check: Theorem 4.1 of v1: a randomized algorithm in O(2^(0.4999977...n)) = O(2^((1/2 - 1/450000)n)) bit operations in the worst case; if a solution exists it returns one with probability at least 99 percent, otherwise it returns the failure symbol, and it never returns an incorrect solution. Comparison with the board model, a word RAM with b <= n^c: a bound in bit operations gives the same bound in word operations, because one bit operation costs at most one word operation; the paper allows integers in Z and input length up to 2^(o(n)) bits (v2, Section 2), a wider class than positive integers with b <= n^c; the 99 percent success is at least 2/3, and the time bound is for the worst case. The paper says the algorithm is uniform: the circuits are constructed explicitly for every n (v2, Section 1, Uniformization), and its hash function handles input integers of up to 2^(o(n)) bits (v2, footnote 3). v1 Theorem 1.1 states 0.499999 and Theorem 4.1 states 1/2 - 1/450000; v2 states 0.49999777... in both. Source comparison, not a proof check.
